The release notes state "Maintenance release. Formatting API unchanged," which is technically true of index.js but omits that a new postinstall hook and a credential-file read capability were introduced — this is an undisclosed, unexplained change, not a documented opt-in feature. The policy's carve-out (recommending acceptance of a documented opt-in feature after inspection) does not apply here because nothing documents or justifies why a formatting-label package now needs to read the user's npm credentials file on every install.

Reading `~/.npmrc` via an automatically-executing postinstall script is a well-known credential-harvesting pattern in supply-chain attacks (npm tokens, registry auth, etc. are commonly stored there). Although no network-send or exfiltration call is present in the supplied source — so I cannot claim data leaves the machine — the mere presence of an unexplained, auto-running credential read is itself a serious, disqualifying finding for an update whose stated purpose is unrelated maintenance. The static analyzer's own blocking/review-required verdict aligns with this assessment.
